tldr: Ella is an embodied social agent with a structured long-term multimodal memory system enabling lifelong learning in a 3D open world through visual observation and social interaction.
contributions: A structured long-term memory with name-centric semantic memory and spatiotemporal episodic memory to support lifelong learning
Ella, the first embodied social agent that self-evolves through visual observation and social interaction by integrating structured memory with foundation models
Capability-oriented experiments in a dynamic 3D open world with 15 agents demonstrating advanced cognitive abilities including social reasoning and leadership
methods: Ella builds a hierarchical scene graph for spatial memory (volume grid, object, and region layers) and a spatiotemporal episodic memory storing events with temporal, spatial, and content attributes. It uses a planning-reaction framework where it retrieves from memory to generate a daily schedule, then processes new observations to revise schedules, interact with the environment, or engage in conversation. The system was evaluated in Virtual Community with 15 agents simulated for 9 hours, followed by controlled evaluations: Influence Battle (persuading agents to attend parties) and Leadership Quest (leading groups to complete tasks under resource constraints).
results: Ella demonstrated advanced cognitive abilities including social reasoning and leadership, showing it can influence, lead, and cooperate with other agents effectively. In Influence Battle, agents were measured by show-up rate and conversation count for party invitations. In Leadership Quest, success was measured by average completion rate and conversation efficacy among group members. Results across three communities showed Ella performs well in these capabilities.
limitations: The paper notes that no prior work studied long-term memory systems learning from both visual observations and social interactions simultaneously. Baseline comparisons are limited to re-implementations of CoELA (originally designed for only two agents in constrained indoor scenes) and Generative Agents (which assume oracle perception and use predefined communication mechanisms), suggesting gaps in comparable embodied social agent frameworks for open 3D worlds.
